paragraphs.en: France, which prides itself as the global innovator of fashion, has decided its fashion industry has lost an absolute right to define physical beauty for women. Its lawmakers gave preliminary approval last week to a law that would make it a crime to employ ultra-thin models on runways. The parliament also agreed to ban websites that “incite excessive thinness” by promoting extreme dieting.
paragraphs.zh: 法国一向以全球时尚创新者自居，如今却认定，本国时尚业已经失去了界定女性形体美的绝对权利。上周，法国立法者初步批准了一项法律，拟将雇用极瘦模特走秀的行为定为犯罪。议会还同意禁止那些通过提倡极端节食来“煽动过度消瘦”的网站。

paragraphs.en: Such measures have a couple of uplifting motives. They suggest beauty should not be defined by looks that end up impinging on health. That’s a start. And the ban on ultra-thin models seems to go beyond protecting models from starving themselves to death – as some have done. It tells the fashion industry that it must take responsibility for the signal it sends women, especially teenage girls, about the social tape-measure they must use to determine their individual worth.
paragraphs.zh: 这些措施有几个令人振奋的出发点。它们表明，人们不应以最终会损害健康的外表来定义美。这是一个开端。而禁止使用极瘦模特，似乎又超出了防止模特把自己饿死的目的——已有一些模特因此丧命。它告诉时尚业，对于它向女性、尤其是少女所传递的信息，即她们必须用来衡量自身价值的社会标准，时尚业必须承担责任。

paragraphs.en: The bans, if fully enforced, would suggest to women (and many men) that they should not let others be arbiters of their beauty. And perhaps faintly, they hint that people should look to intangible qualities like character and intellect rather than dieting their way to size zero or wasp-waist physiques.
paragraphs.zh: 如果这些禁令得到全面执行，就会向女性（以及许多男性）传达这样的意思：她们不应让别人来裁定自己是否美丽。这些禁令或许还隐约暗示，人们应该重视品格、才智等内在品质，而不是靠节食穿上零号服装，或练出蜂腰般的身材。

paragraphs.en: The French measures, however, rely too much on severe punishment to change a culture that still regards beauty as skin-deep – and bone-showing. Under the law, using a fashion model that does not meet a government-defined index of body mass could result in a $85,000 fine and six months in prison.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，法国的措施过度依赖严厉惩罚，来改变一种仍将美停留在表面、并以骨感为美的文化。根据这项法律，雇用体重指数不符合政府规定的时装模特，可能招致8.5万美元的罚款和六个月监禁。

paragraphs.en: The fashion industry knows it has an inherent problem in focusing on material adornment and idealized body types. In Denmark, the United States, and a few other countries, it is trying to set voluntary standards for models and fashion images that rely more on peer pressure for enforcement.
paragraphs.zh: 时尚业知道，它过度关注物质装饰和理想化体型，这本身存在固有问题。在丹麦、美国和少数其他国家，时尚业正尝试为模特和时尚形象制定自愿遵守的标准，更多依靠同行压力来推动执行。

paragraphs.en: In contrast to France’s actions, Denmark’s fashion industry agreed last month on rules and sanctions regarding the age, health, and other characteristics of models. The newly revised Danish Fashion Ethical Charter clearly states: “We are aware of and take responsibility for the impact the fashion industry has on body ideals, especially on young people.” The charter’s main tool of enforcement is to deny access for designers and modeling agencies to Copenhagen Fashion Week (CFW), which is run by the Danish Fashion Institute. But in general it relies on a name-and-shame method of compliance.
paragraphs.zh: 与法国的举措不同，丹麦时尚业上个月就模特的年龄、健康及其他特征，达成了有关规则和制裁措施的协议。新修订的《丹麦时尚道德宪章》明确指出：“我们意识到时尚业对理想体型观念、尤其对年轻人的影响，并愿意对此负责。”该宪章主要的执行手段，是禁止违规设计师和模特经纪机构参加由丹麦时尚学院主办的哥本哈根时装周。不过总体而言，它依靠的是点名曝光、使违规者蒙羞的方式，来促使人们遵守规定。

paragraphs.en: Relying on ethical persuasion rather than law to address the misuse of body ideals may be the best step. Even better would be to help elevate notions of beauty beyond the material standards of a particular industry.
paragraphs.zh: 依靠道德劝导，而不是法律，来解决理想体型观念被滥用的问题，或许是最佳举措。更好的做法则是帮助人们提升对美的认识，使之超越某个特定行业的物质标准。
